task.description:
Step 4b (Test Design Gate) for WF03-ISS0774-20260924. HARD GATE.
Read test/letflow/routers/help_test.exs, specifically the new test added in the tie-break describe.
The new test must: (1) create two rows with timestamps straddling a second boundary, (2) assert the fresher wall-clock row is returned (which the old code would fail ~1% of the time), (3) be the fail-first proof.
Check: test uses real DB rows (not mocks), asserts the correct row, is a genuine regression test for the Erlang structural comparison bug.
Complete handoff (step-04b-test-design-gate.json): COMPLETED, PASS or FAIL.
acceptance_criteria: New regression test exists for the second-boundary case
Test asserts correct (fresher) row is returned
Fail-first proof: old code would fail this

timestamps_straddle_second_boundary.evidence: stale updated_at set to ~U[2024-01-01 00:00:05.999000Z] (second=5, microsecond=999000); fresh updated_at set to ~U[2024-01-01 00:00:06.000001Z] (second=6, microsecond=1). Canonical straddle: higher microsecond on the older second.

asserts_fresh_row_returned.evidence: Line 285: assert json(conn)["id"] == fresh.id -- asserts the later wall-clock row (second=6) is returned.

genuine_fail_first.evidence: Old code was Enum.max_by(many, & &1.updated_at) which uses Erlang structural map comparison. DateTime atoms sorted lexicographically: 'microsecond' < 'second', so microsecond is the first differentiating field. stale.microsecond={999000,6} > fresh.microsecond={1,6}, so old code picks stale. Test asserts fresh -- old code fails. New code Enum.max_by(many, &{DateTime.to_unix(&1.updated_at, :microsecond), &1.id}) converts to integer before comparison: fresh unix_us (6_000_001) > stale unix_us (5_999_000), picks fresh correctly.

real_db_rows_not_mocks.evidence: Uses live!() + Repo.update!(prefix: schema_name) to write real rows; dispatches real HTTP request via build_conn |> dispatch(). No mocks or stubs.

test_count_now_14.evidence: grep found exactly 14 'test "' lines in help_test.exs. New test is test #9 in file order; total went from 13 to 14.

result.summary: All five gate checks PASS. The new test 'when two live rows have the same process_definition_id, the row with the later updated_at wins regardless of microsecond position' is a genuine fail-first regression proof: it would have failed against the old Enum.max_by structural-comparison code and passes against the fixed integer-based comparison. AC1 satisfied.
